data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra, having raised $11.5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which is applicable given Karman's Seed positioning. Using total capital raised ($11.5M) as a proxy base and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression to the next stage yields an implied valuation of $29M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible: while nine same-sector peers exist in the Climate & Energy universe, none of the narrow peer filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—returned the required minimum of three datapoints. A broader all-sector median would introduce excessive dispersion and was therefore excluded.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $24M (low) to $33M (high), with a median of $29M. This single-method approach reflects the inherent constraint of insufficient granular peer data at the Seed stage in this emerging sector. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for Karman's specific risk profile and market conditions, and the absence of transaction comparables that would validate the step-up magnitude. Further data collection or follow-on fundraising milestones would strengthen conviction.
